forces.title: Digital Revolution Fostered 'Free Music' Culture
forces.description: The digital revolution, despite democratizing music access, inadvertently fostered a culture where music is often expected to be free. This shift, from paying for physical formats (LPs, Cassettes, CDs) to relying on 'freemium' ad-supported models or free alternatives like YouTube, has diminished the perceived value of music. This structural change risks weakening the economic foundation for creators and copyright owners, creating a disconnect between unprecedented consumption and scarce willingness to pay for premium experiences.
forces.source_title: How India can unlock the next phase of music streaming growth

forces.title: High Churn Risk from Free Alternatives and Piracy
forces.description: A significant portion of Indian consumers (39% in a survey) would not pay for music under any circumstances, with 70% shifting to free YouTube and 28% moving to pirated sources if all free options were removed. This high price sensitivity, coupled with a perception of music as ambient and substitutable content (unlike video), indicates a substantial risk of user churn if monetization efforts are too aggressive or fail to provide compelling value differentiation. Users actively seek workarounds for friction, further highlighting this challenge.
forces.source_title: How India can unlock the next phase of music streaming growth

forces.title: Lack of Clear Differentiation Between Free and Paid Music Offerings
forces.description: A major barrier to paid music streaming adoption is the perceived lack of differentiation between free and paid products. Many non-paying users feel that free platforms like YouTube adequately meet their needs. This lack of clear value distinction, combined with users switching fluidly across platforms based on use-case rather than loyalty, makes it challenging for digital service providers to convince consumers to subscribe. Strengthening value differentiation through superior quality, seamless functionality, and meaningful exclusivity is critical for monetization.
forces.source_title: How India can unlock the next phase of music streaming growth

forces.title: Bundling Drives Usage Without Perceived Standalone Value
forces.description: While telecom and e-commerce bundles contribute significantly to music streaming usage, they often fail to translate into strong user attachment or perceived standalone value for the music service. Many users access bundled services because they come 'free' (e.g., Amazon Music with Prime). This creates a risk of user dropout if the bundle disappears, rather than conversion to a paid subscription, as the perceived value of music as a 'background utility' remains low. Strategies are needed to convert bundled users into direct, loyal subscribers.
forces.source_title: How India can unlock the next phase of music streaming growth

forces.title: Rapid Economic Growth & Rising Smartphone Penetration Boost Digital Music
forces.description: India's status as the world's fastest-growing major economy (6.5% real GDP growth in 2025, projected US$7.3 trillion by 2030) provides a strong macro tailwind. This is coupled with surging smartphone penetration (584 million in 2025, reaching 735 million by 2030), affordable data plans, and over one billion mobile broadband connections. These factors create a fertile ground for digital music consumption, making India one of the fastest-growing digital music markets globally and driving widespread access to streaming platforms.
forces.source_title: How India can unlock the next phase of music streaming growth

forces.title: Affordable Data & Young Demographics Drive Digital Consumption
forces.description: India boasts some of the lowest data charges globally, coupled with over a billion active mobile broadband connections. This widespread and affordable connectivity significantly lowers the barrier to digital content consumption, including music streaming. Furthermore, a predominantly young population (65% under 35 years of age) is a key driver of digital adoption and engagement, translating into high daily music listening habits across smartphones and streaming platforms. These demographic and connectivity factors fuel the expansion of the digital music market.
forces.source_title: How India can unlock the next phase of music streaming growth

forces.title: Expanding Vehicle Base Fuels In-Car Music Consumption
forces.description: India's rapidly expanding vehicle base, with over 400 million registered vehicles as of 2025 and passenger vehicle dispatches growing significantly (25.4% YoY in April 2026), acts as a structural driver for music consumption. Music often serves as high-energy content during commuting, and the increase in private mobility creates more opportunities for in-car listening. This expands the use-case scenarios for digital music services beyond personal devices, contributing to overall engagement and potential for monetization.
forces.source_title: How India can unlock the next phase of music streaming growth

forces.title: Live Entertainment as Economic Multiplier for Tourism
forces.description: Live entertainment is undergoing a significant transformation in India, moving beyond standalone cultural events to become a powerful economic platform. Concerts and large-format events are now acting as economic multipliers, capable of driving tourism, activating local businesses across hospitality, transport, and retail, and enhancing regional visibility. This shift is turning live entertainment into a strategic growth lever for cities and regions, generating impacts that extend well beyond the event itself by integrating into broader leisure and travel decisions of younger audiences.
forces.source_title: The Assam report: Turning live music economy into a tourism multiplier

forces.title: Government Policy Support for Concert Tourism
forces.description: Government bodies, such as the Assam Tourism Development Corporation, are proactively positioning live entertainment as an engine of economic growth. This includes the introduction of Concert Tourism Policies with financial and logistical support (e.g., Viability Gap Funding, venue access, security coordination), designation of nodal agencies for single-window facilitation, and regulatory refinements. Such policy backing significantly reduces execution friction for organizers, attracts global-scale events, and helps states institutionalize live entertainment as a repeatable economic driver, fostering tourism and local employment.
forces.source_title: The Assam report: Turning live music economy into a tourism multiplier

forces.title: Strong Economic Multiplier Effect of Live Events
forces.description: Live events demonstrate a significant economic multiplier effect, typically generating nearly three times the incremental local spend for every INR1 of ticket revenue. This impact extends across various sectors, including hospitality (increased occupancy and tariffs), transport (higher ride demand), F&B (increased footfall and average bill value), and retail (concert-specific purchases, local shopping). Beyond direct spending, events also boost GST collections, create temporary employment opportunities for a large workforce (e.g., 2,500 personnel for Post Malone concert), and generate local business for vendors, supporting overall urban economic activation.
forces.source_title: The Assam report: Turning live music economy into a tourism multiplier

forces.title: Improved Air Routes & Connectivity Enhance Accessibility for Live Events
forces.description: Enhanced connectivity, including improved air routes, highway upgrades, and intra-city mobility, is a key structural factor accelerating the live entertainment market. Better accessibility benefits both artists and audiences, drawing attendees from diverse geographies (over 200 cities across India and internationally for Assam events). Airport upgrades and regional connectivity facilitate travel, reducing logistical hurdles and increasing the potential audience pool for large-scale events. This improved infrastructure supports the emergence of non-metro cities as viable concert destinations.
forces.source_title: The Assam report: Turning live music economy into a tourism multiplier

forces.title: New Hotel Development Strengthens Hospitality Capacity for Events
forces.description: The growth in hospitality infrastructure, particularly the entry of new hotels (including international five-star brands and mid-to-premium options) in emerging concert hubs like Guwahati, is a significant tailwind. This increased accommodation capacity is crucial for supporting year-round large-scale events and handling the demand surges during concert weekends. Adequate lodging facilitates extended stays by visitors, maximizing tourism spillover effects and ensuring a better overall experience for attendees, which in turn boosts promoter confidence and destination readiness.
forces.source_title: The Assam report: Turning live music economy into a tourism multiplier

forces.title: Large Youth Population with Digital Ticketing Affinity
forces.description: India's demographic advantage, characterized by a large youth population with increasing digital ticketing adoption and affinity for global music formats, reinforces the momentum of the live entertainment market. This segment is highly engaged, driving rising online ticket purchases and diverse genre attendance across live events. Their willingness to travel for experiences and integrate events into broader leisure decisions fuels demand, making non-metro markets with strong youth participation particularly attractive for promoters and artists.
forces.source_title: The Assam report: Turning live music economy into a tourism multiplier

forces.title: Live Events Create Large-Scale Temporary Employment & Local Business Opportunities
forces.description: Large-format live events act as significant generators of temporary employment, mobilizing substantial workforces across operational, technical, and service functions (e.g., 2,500 personnel for a single concert). These opportunities span skilled and semi-skilled roles in venue operations, security, hospitality, logistics, and F&B, providing incremental income for local workers. Additionally, a significant proportion of services are sourced from local vendors and regional partners, facilitating broader economic participation, capability building, and reducing reliance on external production ecosystems, contributing to the formalization of the event supply chain.
forces.source_title: The Assam report: Turning live music economy into a tourism multiplier

forces.title: Institutionalizing Public-Private Partnerships for Event Execution
forces.description: The success of large-scale live entertainment, particularly in emerging markets, hinges on institutionalizing structured public-private partnerships. Collaborations between government (providing venues, security, mobility, and subsidies) and experienced platforms (leading curation, logistics, ticketing, marketing) combine private-sector execution capability with public-sector facilitation. These frameworks accelerate execution, attract global artists by reducing market-entry risk and signaling destination readiness, and improve promoter confidence, leading to predictable programming and faster activation cycles. Shared accountability for economic outcomes enhances the long-term viability of the concert economy.
forces.source_title: The Assam report: Turning live music economy into a tourism multiplier

forces.title: Creating Predictable Approval Frameworks & Nodal Ownership
forces.description: Execution certainty is a critical success factor for large-format live events. States establishing predictable approval frameworks, single-window facilitation, and designating nodal agencies for inter-departmental coordination significantly reduce friction across licensing, permissions, law and order, traffic management, and venue access. Clear institutional ownership enables faster decision-making and minimizes coordination delays, which is paramount for attracting repeat investments from promoters and global talent. Standardized operating playbooks allow states to move from reactive event management to proactive capacity planning, ensuring smooth event delivery and enhancing destination attractiveness.
forces.source_title: The Assam report: Turning live music economy into a tourism multiplier

forces.title: Rising Per Capita Income Drives Ticketed Events Growth
forces.description: Rising per capita incomes and the expansion of India's middle class are significant drivers for the growth of ticketed events, including music concerts, comedy performances, and sports. As individuals' discretionary spending capacity increases, their propensity to spend on entertainment and value-added services rises. This economic trend fosters a larger consumer base willing to pay for live experiences, contributing to the steady growth of the live entertainment sector and enabling higher revenue generation from ticketing and associated services.
forces.source_title: Media and Entertainment Industry In India

viewpoints.title: Indian Music Market: High Consumption, Low Monetization, Urgent Need for Subscriptions
viewpoints.description: EY, in collaboration with IMI, highlights a paradox in India's music industry: unprecedented consumption levels despite diminished perceived value. While 96% of smartphone users listen daily, monetization remains under-penetrated, creating a disconnect between consumption and compensation. A robust subscription ecosystem is essential to fuel creativity, drive investment, nurture talent, and expand Indian music's global cultural footprint. The industry must balance innovation, differentiation, and consumer awareness to unlock significant growth in paid music consumption and redefine music's value.
viewpoints.source_title: How India can unlock the next phase of music streaming growth

viewpoints.title: Digital Music at Inflection Point: Elevate Value, Differentiate Paid, Integrate Experiences
viewpoints.description: EY identifies India's digital music market at a critical inflection point due to deep, universal engagement contrasting with significant under-monetization. To seize this generational opportunity, the industry must fundamentally reshape consumer perception of music's value. Three priorities are crucial: elevating music from a background utility to a premium offering, creating clear differentiation between free and paid experiences (quality, functionality, exclusivity), and innovating beyond traditional listening to build richer, integrated experiences with social interaction, live events, and the creator economy. Strong digital foundations, bundling, and partnerships are expected to expand the paid subscriber base.
viewpoints.source_title: How India can unlock the next phase of music streaming growth

viewpoints.title: Digitization Fosters 'Free Music' Culture, Threatening Creator Economy Sustainability
viewpoints.description: IMI emphasizes that while digitization has democratized music access, it has inadvertently fostered a 'free music' culture, leading to astonishingly scarce willingness to pay compared to the physical era. This non-paid ecosystem negatively impacts creators and copyright owners, the epicenter of the music industry. Record labels, digital service providers, and creators must collaborate towards a tiered paid ecosystem to provide economic oxygen for artists, fund new projects, and support the broader value chain, including local audio engineers and studios.
viewpoints.source_title: How India can unlock the next phase of music streaming growth

viewpoints.title: Live Entertainment Transforming into Economic Multiplier for Emerging Cities
viewpoints.description: EY observes a significant transformation in India's live entertainment, with concerts increasingly shaping the economic momentum and identity of emerging cities beyond metros. Live entertainment is evolving into an economic platform capable of driving tourism, activating local businesses, and enhancing regional visibility. Concerts generate economic impacts far beyond the event itself, benefiting hospitality, transport, retail, and dining. Coordinated planning and ecosystem collaboration, as exemplified by the Post Malone concert in Guwahati, demonstrate how live events can serve as strategic growth levers when government, platform partners, and local ecosystems align.
viewpoints.source_title: The Assam report: Turning live music economy into a tourism multiplier

viewpoints.title: India's Live Entertainment Entering New Growth Phase with Concerts as Repeatable Economic Drivers
viewpoints.description: EY states India's live entertainment industry is poised for a new growth phase, transforming concerts into repeatable economic drivers, particularly for emerging cities. This trend is fueled by younger audiences integrating live events into broader leisure and travel decisions, spending across multiple sectors. Realizing this potential, however, necessitates enabling policy frameworks, institutional coordination, and strong public-private collaboration. States aligning tourism strategy, infrastructure readiness, and industry partnerships are successfully converting live events into structured economic opportunities, fostering long-term destination visibility and local business activity.
viewpoints.source_title: The Assam report: Turning live music economy into a tourism multiplier
